Understanding the Procedure

What is Laparoscopic Hernia Repair?

Laparoscopic hernia repair is a minimally invasive surgical technique where the surgeon makes several small incisions (usually 0.5–1 cm) instead of one large incision. A laparoscope (a thin tube with a camera) is inserted through one of the incisions, providing a magnified view of the surgical area on a monitor.

Specialised instruments are inserted through the other incisions to repair the hernia. A synthetic mesh is typically placed over the hernia defect and secured with sutures, staples, or tackers to reinforce the abdominal wall.

Key Advantages

Small, barely visible scars
Less post-operative pain
Faster return to daily activities
Same-day or next-day discharge

Keyhole Precision

High-Tech Anesthesia & Micro-Tools

Surgical Variations

Types of Laparoscopic Approaches

There are several tailored minimally invasive options. Dr. Kumar applies specific entry methods based on your physical assessment and diagnostic scans.

Groin Focus

TEP (Totally Extraperitoneal)

The mesh is placed entirely outside the peritoneal cavity in the preperitoneal space, ensuring abdominal organs are not touched.

Learn about TEP
High Visibility

TAPP (Transabdominal Preperitoneal)

The peritoneum is briefly entered to place mesh behind it, allowing comprehensive pelvic visualization to address other findings.

Learn about TAPP
Complex Repair

eTEP (Extended View TEP)

An advanced method providing large extraperitoneal workspaces, allowing keyhole repairs of large or complex abdominal wall hernias.

Learn about eTEP
Why Choose Laparoscopic?

Benefits Over
Open Surgery

Laparoscopic hernia repair offers significant clinical advantages compared to traditional open surgery, making it the preferred choice for most patients.

Gold Standard Accuracy

Approved by Global Surgical Bodies

Smaller Incisions

Only 3 small keyhole incisions (0.5–1 cm) compared to a 3–6 inch incision in open surgery, yielding minimal scarring.

Faster Recovery

Most patients return to normal activities within 1–2 weeks, compared to 3–6 weeks with traditional open surgery.

Less Pain

Minimally invasive keyhole surgical entry means less tissue damage, resulting in significantly lower post-operative discomfort.

Day Care Surgery

Most laparoscopic hernia repairs are performed as day-care surgery, allowing same-day or next-day discharge.

Lower Infection Risk

Smaller incision entry fields limit environmental exposure of deep internal tissues, reducing risks of surgical site infections.

Bilateral Repair

Both left and right side groin hernias can be easily repaired through the same three keyhole incisions in one setting.

Laparoscopic vs Open Surgery: Quick Comparison

Laparoscopic Repair

3 small keyhole incisions (0.5 - 1 cm)
Day daycare surgery or 1-night stay
1–2 weeks average recovery
Minimal post-operative pain
Excellent aesthetic, barely visible scars

Open Surgery

Single larger incision (3–6 inches)
1–3 days hospitalization stay
3–6 weeks total recovery
Moderate to significant post-op pain
More visible, larger surgical scar
The Procedure

How Laparoscopic Hernia Repair Works

Understanding the procedure can help ease any anxiety about surgery. Here's what happens during laparoscopic hernia repair.

1

Anaesthesia

General anaesthesia is administered, so you'll be asleep and pain-free throughout the procedure.

2

Incisions

Three small incisions (5–10 mm each) are made in the abdomen. Carbon dioxide gas inflates the abdomen for better visibility.

3

Repair

The laparoscope guides the surgeon to gently push the hernia back and place a sterile mesh over the defect.

4

Closure

The mesh is secured, gas is released, and small incisions are closed with sutures or surgical glue.

Duration of Surgery

The procedure typically takes 30–90 minutes depending on the type and complexity of hernia. Most patients spend 2–4 hours in the hospital including recovery time.

Healing Journey

Recovery Timeline

Recovery from laparoscopic hernia repair is typically faster and more comfortable than open surgery. Here's what to expect.

Day 1–3

Initial Recovery

  • Mild pain at incision sites
  • Rest but walk regularly
  • Same or next-day discharge
Week 1

At Home

  • Resume light activities
  • Avoid lifting >5 kg
  • Desk work acceptable
Weeks 2–4

Building Strength

  • Light exercise OK
  • Most restrictions lifted
  • Normal daily activities
Weeks 4–6

Full Recovery

  • Heavy lifting OK
  • Return to exercise
  • Complete healing

Important Recovery Notes

Do's

  • ✓ Walk regularly to promote blood circulation and reduce risks of vascular clots.
  • ✓ Keep the three miniature incision sites completely clean and dry.
  • ✓ Follow surgical directives on wound dressings and follow-up care.
  • ✓ Attend scheduled postoperative checkup consultations promptly.

Don'ts

  • ✗ Do not lift items heavier than 5 kg (e.g. heavy luggage) for 4–6 weeks.
  • ✗ Avoid strenuous high-impact jogging, gym weight training, or core exercises.
  • ✗ Do not operate motor vehicles while actively taking prescription pain relievers.
  • ✗ Avoid soaking in bathtubs or swimming pools until surgical scars close.
Making the Choice

Choosing the Right Technique

Dr. Kumar will recommend the most suitable approach based on your specific condition. Here's how laparoscopic repair compares to other techniques.

Technique Best For Recovery Scarring
Laparoscopic (Standard) Most primary hernias, bilateral repairs 1–2 weeks 3 small keyholes
TEP Groin hernias, avoiding peritoneal entry 1–2 weeks 3 small keyholes
TAPP Hernias requiring full pelvic inspection 1–2 weeks 3 small keyholes
eTEP Complex, large, or recurrent hernias 2–4 weeks Small keyholes
Open Repair Very large hernias, not candidates for laparoscopy 3–6 weeks Single larger incision

🤷‍♂️ FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Most laparoscopic hernia repairs take between 30 and 90 minutes depending on the type and complexity. Bilateral (both sides) repairs naturally take longer. Total time in hospital, including preparation and recovery from anaesthesia, is usually 3–5 hours.

For desk-based work, most patients return within 5–7 days. For physically demanding jobs involving lifting or manual labour, a 3–4 week break is recommended. Dr. Kumar will provide a specific timeline based on your job type and recovery progress.

Yes — this is one of the biggest advantages of laparoscopic hernia repair. Both left and right groin hernias can be repaired through the same three small incisions in a single operation, avoiding the need for two separate surgeries.

Laparoscopic hernia repair is a well-established procedure with an excellent safety record. Serious complications are rare (less than 1%). The minimally invasive approach actually reduces infection risk compared to open surgery. Dr. Kumar will discuss your specific risk profile during consultation.

Laparoscopic surgery leaves only 3 very small marks (5–10 mm) which typically fade to barely visible marks within 6–12 months. This is a dramatic improvement over the 3–6 inch scar left by open hernia surgery. Most patients are very pleased with the cosmetic result.

Laparoscopic hernia repair with mesh has an excellent recurrence rate of less than 1–2%, similar to open mesh repair. Without mesh, recurrence rates are significantly higher (over 20%). Dr. Kumar uses only high-quality, FDA-approved meshes for durable, long-lasting repairs.
